apollo11.panorama_caption: Tranquility Base, EVA-1. Buzz Aldrin photographed the LM Eagle and the U.S. flag soon after landing. Visible Hasselblad seams + chromatic stitching at the LM are part of the published mosaic.

panorama_annotations.label: LM Eagle
panorama_annotations.body: Descent stage of the Lunar Module, where Armstrong + Aldrin stood for the EVA.

panorama_annotations.label: U.S. flag
panorama_annotations.body: Planted ~8 m west of the LM. Knocked over by the ascent stage exhaust on lift-off.

panorama_annotations.label: Buzz Aldrin shadow
panorama_annotations.body: Photographer's own shadow in the foreground — Buzz holding the Hasselblad.

apollo17.panorama_caption: Taurus-Littrow valley, Station 5. Schmitt + Cernan worked Camelot Crater and the South Massif here. Final lunar EVA panorama in the Apollo programme.

panorama_annotations.label: South Massif
panorama_annotations.body: 2.3 km uplifted highland, sampled at Station 2 (the orange-soil discovery site).

panorama_annotations.label: Camelot Crater rim
panorama_annotations.body: Large pre-existing impact crater near the Lunar Module; Station 5 boulder field is on the rim.

panorama_annotations.label: Lunar Roving Vehicle
panorama_annotations.body: The third LRV used on the Moon. Total traverse this mission: 35.7 km — still the record.

spirit.panorama_caption: Spirit's view from the summit of Husband Hill — first Martian summit reached by a rover. Looking south across the Inner Basin of Gusev Crater toward the Columbia Hills.

opportunity.panorama_caption: Opportunity's view from inside Eagle Crater, the airbag-bounce landing site — the layered Burns Cliff outcrop visible across the crater wall would become the rover's first major science target.

curiosity.panorama_caption: Curiosity at Gediz Vallis Channel — the rover's 360° view from sol 4220 after drilling the Mammoth Lakes sample, its 41st on Mars. Robotic arm visible at left, just finished drilling; rover deck on the right; real Martian sky in the upper band; Gediz Vallis channel descending through the centre — first place pure sulfur crystals were ever found on Mars.

panorama_annotations.label: Gediz Vallis channel
panorama_annotations.body: Ancient water-carved channel descending Mt. Sharp's slopes. Curiosity drilled the Mammoth Lakes sample here — first pure sulfur crystals ever found on Mars.

panorama_annotations.label: Robotic arm
panorama_annotations.body: 2 m articulated arm with the drill, brush, and APXS spectrometer — visible at left after completing the Mammoth Lakes drill on this sol.

panorama_annotations.label: Mt. Sharp lower flank
panorama_annotations.body: Layered slopes of Aeolis Mons, the 5 km mountain at the centre of Gale Crater that Curiosity has been climbing since 2014.

perseverance.panorama_caption: First 360° panorama from Perseverance — three days after landing. The rover deck dominates the foreground; Jezero crater floor + the distant rim are visible above the horizon; real Martian sky in the upper bands.

panorama_annotations.label: Mastcam-Z mast
panorama_annotations.body: The 2 m camera mast — the rover's own "eyes" — visible in the centre because the panorama wraps around it.

panorama_annotations.label: Jezero crater rim
panorama_annotations.body: The crater wall ~2 km away; ancient delta deposits are visible at this rim's western edge — the science target Perseverance drove toward over its first year.

panorama_annotations.label: Rover deck
panorama_annotations.body: Foreground of every Mastcam-Z 360° — solar-panel-style deck, sample-tube cache visible at right.

mars3.panorama_caption: First Mars soft landing — 14.5 seconds of transmitted scan data before signal lost. There is no Tier-3 panorama to render at this site (yet); the experience here is the honest-historical-artifact framing of the original fragment via the Tier-2 CTX context.

change4.panorama_caption: First panorama ever transmitted from the lunar farside. Von Kármán crater within South Pole–Aitken Basin. Yutu-2 rover visible mid-distance; lander shadow lower-left.

panorama_annotations.label: Yutu-2 rover
panorama_annotations.body: First rover on the lunar farside; still operational at 5+ years (the record for any lunar rover).

panorama_annotations.label: Von Kármán crater rim
panorama_annotations.body: Inner rim of the 180 km crater inside the South Pole–Aitken Basin — the Moon's largest, oldest impact structure.

panorama_annotations.label: Chang'e 4 lander shadow
panorama_annotations.body: The lander's own shadow on the regolith — captured by its onboard terrain camera.

chandrayaan3.panorama_caption: Shiv Shakti Point — first panorama from the lunar south pole. Vikram lander shadow visible foreground; Pragyan rover deployed onto the regolith shortly after this image.

panorama_annotations.label: Pragyan rover (deployed sol +1)
panorama_annotations.body: 26 kg six-wheeled rover. Deployed via Vikram's ramp the day after landing; operated until lunar nightfall (~14 Earth days).

panorama_annotations.label: South pole crater rim
panorama_annotations.body: First successful soft-landing this close to the lunar south pole — water-ice prospect zone.

vandenberg-slc-4e.panorama_caption: Vandenberg SLC-4E (Falcon 9) and SLC-4W from the air — an aerial view, not a ground-level panorama.
vandenberg-slc-4e.compass_zero_direction: photo centre (true compass orientation not calibrated)

baikonur-1-5.panorama_caption: Gagarin's Start (Site 1/5) before the Soyuz TMA-13 rollout — a very low-resolution banner crop.
baikonur-1-5.compass_zero_direction: photo centre (true compass orientation not calibrated)

baikonur-31-6.panorama_caption: Baikonur Site 31/6 from the top of the Soyuz service structure — the pad flame trench below, the steppe and the Zenit facility on the horizon.
baikonur-31-6.compass_zero_direction: photo centre (true compass orientation not calibrated)

jiuquan-slc-43.panorama_caption: Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center main launch tower from a distance — a low-resolution panoramic strip across the Gobi.
jiuquan-slc-43.compass_zero_direction: photo centre (true compass orientation not calibrated)

wenchang-lc-101.panorama_caption: Wenchang launch site across Qishui Bay — the LC-101 towers seen from the beach, a distant shoreline view.
wenchang-lc-101.compass_zero_direction: photo centre (true compass orientation not calibrated)

sriharikota-slp.panorama_caption: Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota — PSLV-C61 in transit from the Vehicle Integration Facility toward the launch pad.
sriharikota-slp.compass_zero_direction: photo centre (true compass orientation not calibrated)
